gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long each bank actually holds 140 W from one port: ChargerLAB's AOHi Future Starship 240W shut off after 10 min under a constant 140 W load (temperature protection, 24.06 Wh delivered), techtest.org's Anker Prime 26K 300W held a constant 140 W per port, and techtest.org's UGREEN Nexode 165W (built-in cables, PB552) held 140 W for about half its charge before dropping to 65 W.
standout_why: I opened the cited rival pages. Popular Science (updated 2026-10-26) says outright that it gives no measured wattage for any pick and no measured efficiency. Its only test numbers are phone and iPad charge percentages for the older UGREEN 100W model. Wirecutter via the proxy (updated 2026-04-13) lists only rated port watts, capacity and weight. The Expert Reviews roundup (updated 2026-11-11) measures the UGREEN PB771 (98 W + 42 W) and the Anker A1695 (laptop 0–30% in 21 min) but gives no measured figure for the Anker Prime A110A and no usable-capacity numbers. Android Central's page came back with only its title. Wired was blocked to my fetcher, so I could not check it. None of the pages I could read reports usable Wh, sustained 140 W, or thermal cut-off for the candidates.
decides: This changes the pick. Our page lists the AOHi first and claims '140 W (either USB-C)'. In ChargerLAB's test, the AOHi delivers 140 W for only about 10 minutes and 100 W for 23 minutes before temperature protection stops it. Two different reviewers (Michael Barton at techtest.org and Stuart Andrews at Expert Reviews) measured the Anker Prime 26K at a steady 140 W and 137.6 W, and it refilled in 48 min (techtest.org) or reached 88.7% in 30 min (Expert Reviews). That supports the Anker Prime as the pick for fast laptop charging. The UGREEN 165W with built-in cables is the cheaper option that holds 140 W for about half its charge. The UGREEN 130W should be described as a 100 W bank that drops to 65 W at 34% left. Caveat: ChargerLAB and techtest.org use different load rigs and conditions, so the AOHi and Anker results are not from one identical test.
